analysis.overall: You had a fantastic day with 96% time in range and an average glucose of 119 mg/dL. Aside from a delayed rise after dinner, your system handled meals and overnight corrections smoothly.

events.title: Lunch bolus dip
events.description: Taking your meal bolus while glucose was already drifting down caused a brief dip to 64 mg/dL before the 50g of carbs kicked in and leveled you out.

events.title: Afternoon steep drop
events.description: Insulin for a 20g snack pulled your glucose down quickly from 175 mg/dL to 68 mg/dL over an hour, though a quick temp target helped prevent a deeper low.

events.title: Dinner's delayed peak
events.description: Carbs eaten in two waves caused an initial dip followed by a late rise to 199 mg/dL around 9:45 PM, which needed a few small corrections to bring down.

events.title: Steady overnight line
events.description: Small automated corrections gently flattened a slight 2 AM bump, keeping you comfortably between 90 and 130 mg/dL until morning.

events.title: Late morning breakfast
events.description: A 30g carb meal and 2u bolus brought your low-ish morning baseline smoothly up to rest near 155 mg/dL.

analysis.watch_for_tomorrow: Dinner carbs took longer than expected to digest, causing an early drop followed by a late peak—consider splitting or delaying your meal bolus.
